---
title: "Allocation dynamics (hotspots and resource allocation)"
toc: true
---

## What it is
Allocation models study how an enforcer distributes scarce resources across space and time, under uncertainty and strategic response.

---

## Canonical two-location baseline
Allocate effort $e_A,e_B\ge 0$ with:
$$
e_A + e_B \le E.
$$
Crime intensity in location $\ell$ decreases in effort: $\lambda_\ell(e_\ell)\downarrow$,
but offenders may substitute across locations.

---

## Why dynamics matters
In practice:
- the enforcer learns where problems are (updating beliefs),
- offenders adapt to allocation patterns,
- recorded crime reflects both incidence and reporting.

Dynamic primitives:
- belief state about each location,
- learning/updating,
- offender adaptation,
- objective function (harm vs recorded metrics).

---

## Predictions (qualitative)
- allocate to high marginal return hotspots, but displacement can occur when substitution is easy
- exploration–exploitation arises when learning is valuable
- metrics can distort allocation if they reward recorded outcomes
